evidence.assay_type: OECD TG 406 (guinea pig skin sensitisation test)
evidence.experimental_conditions: Twenty male Hartley guinea pigs; induction 6 h/week for 3 weeks (days 1, 8, 15) with 0.9% saline + 0.25 g graphene; on day 29 challenge during 6 h with 0.9% saline + 0.25 g graphene; epicutaneous exposure with occlusive wrap. Control group and positive control group (α-hexylcinnamaldehyde) included.
evidence.support_text: The REACH registration dossier for graphene platelets (thickness 0.350–0.380 nm, C/O ratio 96/4, surface area 750 m²/g, density 0.2 g/ml, lateral dimension <2 µm, thickness 20–30 layers) included a skin sensitisation study following OECD TG 406. Twenty male Hartley guinea pigs were induced 6 h/week for 3 weeks with 0.9% saline + 0.25 g graphene and challenged on day 29 with the same preparation. No test substance-related clinical observations or body weight alterations were noted. No indication of skin sensitisation was observed at 24 or 48 h after challenge, while the α-hexylcinnamaldehyde positive control induced sensitisation. Thus, graphene is not a skin sensitiser under these conditions.
